html:
The Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes are a union of the Bitterroot Salish, the Pend d'Oreille and the Ktunaxa (Kootenai), with their reservation around Flathead Lake in western Montana. The map shows a wide area of western Montana, their older hunting and living lands.

The Salish, whom outsiders wrongly called Flatheads, lived in the Bitterroot Valley and crossed the mountains to hunt bison on the plains, often fighting the Blackfoot. They welcomed the Lewis and Clark Expedition in 1805 and later asked for Jesuit missionaries. In the Hellgate Treaty of 1855 the tribes ceded most of their land. The Bitterroot Salish were forced north to the reservation in 1891, and in 1910 the US opened the reservation to white homesteaders. The tribes run their own government and the Kerr Dam today. See also Salish and Kootenai Tribes.
